q: Priority Sector Lending requires banks to lend a specified share of their credit to
options: Sectors like agriculture and MSMEs that may not otherwise get timely and adequate credit
Only large corporates with the best credit ratings
explain: PSL is a special dispensation so that sectors such as agriculture and small enterprises are not starved of credit.

q: Which authority assigns banks their priority sector lending obligations?
explain: The RBI gives banks the role of lending a specified portion of their credit to priority sectors.

q: How many categories are listed under priority sector lending in the study material?
explain: The categories are agriculture, MSME, export credit, education, housing, social infrastructure, renewable energy and others.

q: Which of the following would NOT be classified as priority sector lending?
options: Loan to a farmer for buying a tractor
Auto loan for buying a personal car
Education loan within the permitted limit
Housing loan within the prescribed limit
explain: Car loans, consumer durables and gold for a marriage are ordinary retail loans; tractor, education and housing loans within limits qualify.

q: Which set contains only categories recognised under priority sector lending?
options: Agriculture, auto loans, consumer durables and housing
Agriculture, MSME, export credit and education
MSME, share trading, export credit and education
Education, housing, gold for marriages and renewable energy
explain: Each wrong set includes a non-priority item: auto loans, consumer durables, share trading or gold for marriages.

q: What is the overall priority sector lending target as a percentage of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) as given in the study material?
explain: The total priority sector target is 40% of ANBC; 18% is the agriculture sub-target.

q: The abbreviation ANBC used in priority sector targets stands for
explain: Targets are set as a percentage of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) or CEOBE, whichever is higher.

q: What is the target for agriculture lending as a share of ANBC?
explain: Agriculture gets an 18% of ANBC target; 8% of ANBC within it is for small and marginal farmers.

q: Within the agriculture target, what share of ANBC is prescribed for small and marginal farmers?
explain: The 8% sub-target sits inside the 18% agriculture target.

q: What is the sub-target for lending to micro enterprises?
explain: Micro enterprises have a 7.5% target and weaker sections 10%. 8% belongs to small and marginal farmers.

q: What share of ANBC is the target for advances to weaker sections?
explain: Weaker sections have a 10% of ANBC target.

q: The abbreviation CEOBE stands for
options: Capital Equivalent of Overseas Bank Exposure
Credit Equivalent Amount of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure
explain: For PSL purposes, ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher, is the base for targets.

q: From FY 2018-19, which sub-target of 8% of ANBC or CEOBE was extended to foreign banks with 20 branches and above?
options: Lending to small and marginal farmers
explain: The 8% sub-target for small and marginal farmers (and the 7.5% micro-enterprise sub-target) apply to foreign banks with 20 or more branches.

q: As per the MSMED Act 2006 limits in the study material, a manufacturing micro enterprise has an investment in plant and machinery that does not exceed
explain: Manufacturing: micro up to Rs 25 lakh, small up to Rs 5 crore, medium up to Rs 10 crore.

q: A small manufacturing enterprise has investment in plant and machinery of more than Rs 25 lakh but not more than
explain: Small manufacturing units go up to Rs 5 crore; Rs 10 crore is the medium ceiling.

q: A service-sector micro enterprise has investment in equipment that does not exceed
explain: Service sector: micro up to Rs 10 lakh, small up to Rs 2 crore, medium up to Rs 5 crore.

q: A medium service enterprise has investment in equipment of more than Rs 2 crore but not more than
explain: Rs 10 crore is the medium ceiling for manufacturing, not services.

q: Manufacturing enterprises are classified by investment in plant and machinery, while service enterprises are classified by investment in
explain: Under the MSMED Act 2006, service units are defined by investment in equipment.

q: Bank loans to MSMEs engaged in services qualify as priority sector irrespective of loan limits with effect from
explain: The earlier caps of Rs 5 crore and Rs 10 crore for service micro and small/medium units were removed from 1 March 2018.

q: Loans to farmers against pledge or hypothecation of agricultural produce (including warehouse receipts) qualify up to what amount for not more than 12 months?
explain: The limit is Rs 50 lakh for a period not exceeding 12 months.

q: Loans for purchase of land for agricultural purposes qualify as priority sector when given to
explain: Land-purchase loans are eligible only for small and marginal farmers.

q: Loans to corporate farmers and farmer producer organisations engaged in agriculture and allied activities qualify up to an aggregate limit per borrower of
explain: Corporate farmers and FPOs have an aggregate limit of Rs 2 crore per borrower.

q: Which of the following is a farm credit activity eligible under priority sector lending?
options: Loan to buy a car for the farmer's family
Loan to buy gold for a wedding
Loan to a farmer under the Kisan Credit Card Scheme
explain: KCC loans are part of eligible farm credit, along with crop loans and medium or long-term loans for machinery and irrigation.

q: For agriculture infrastructure loans such as storage facilities and soil conservation, the aggregate sanctioned limit per borrower is
explain: Agriculture infrastructure loans are capped at Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system.

q: Loans to cooperative societies of farmers for disposing of the produce of their members are eligible up to
explain: Cooperative societies of farmers can get up to Rs 5 crore for marketing members' produce.

q: Loans for food and agro-processing qualify up to an aggregate sanctioned limit per borrower of
explain: Food and agro-processing has the same Rs 100 crore limit as agriculture infrastructure.

q: Outstanding deposits under RIDF with which institution can be counted for priority sector shortfall?
explain: Deposits under RIDF and other eligible funds with NABARD can be used to cover a priority sector shortfall.

q: Custom Service Units that keep fleets of tractors, threshers and combines and do farm work on contract are covered under which agriculture sub-category?
explain: Custom Service Units are an ancillary activity along with Agriclinics, agribusiness centres and agro-processing.

q: For domestic banks, incremental export credit qualifies as priority sector up to what share of ANBC or CEOBE (whichever is higher)?
explain: Domestic banks get 2% of ANBC or CEOBE for incremental export credit, with a Rs 40 crore per borrower cap.

q: Foreign banks with fewer than 20 branches can count export credit up to what share of ANBC or CEOBE?
explain: Smaller foreign banks have a much larger export credit allowance (32%) than domestic banks (2% of incremental credit).

q: What is the per-borrower sanctioned limit for incremental export credit under priority sector for domestic banks?
explain: The incremental export credit of domestic banks is subject to a sanctioned limit of up to Rs 40 crore per borrower.

q: Bank loans up to what limit per borrower for social infrastructure (schools, health care, drinking water, sanitation) in Tier II to Tier VI centres qualify as priority sector?
explain: The limit is Rs 50 million, that is Rs 5 crore, per borrower.

q: For renewable energy projects such as solar, biomass, wind and micro-hydel, the loan limit per borrower is
explain: The limit is Rs 150 million (Rs 15 crore); for individual households it is Rs 10 lakh.

q: For individual households, the renewable energy loan limit per borrower is
explain: Households can borrow up to Rs 1 million (Rs 10 lakh) for renewable energy.

q: Education loans to individuals, including vocational courses, qualify as priority sector irrespective of the sanctioned amount up to
explain: Education loans qualify up to Rs 20 lakh (Rs 2 million).

q: In metropolitan centres (population of ten lakh and above), housing loans to individuals qualify as priority sector up to
explain: Metro housing loans are eligible up to Rs 35 lakh provided the dwelling unit costs no more than Rs 45 lakh.

q: In centres other than metros, housing loans qualify up to Rs 25 lakh provided the overall cost of the dwelling unit does not exceed
explain: Other centres: loan up to Rs 25 lakh and cost up to Rs 30 lakh. Metros: Rs 35 lakh and Rs 45 lakh.

q: Housing loans given by a bank to its own employees are
options: Not eligible for priority sector classification
Eligible up to Rs 35 lakh in metros
Eligible only in Tier II centres
explain: Housing loans to a bank's own employees are excluded from priority sector.

q: Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs) allow banks to
options: Transfer their loan portfolio and credit risk to another bank
Raise capital from the stock market
Lend at a lower interest rate
Meet priority sector targets by buying certificates when they fall short
explain: Banks with a shortfall buy PSLCs; banks with surplus sell their excess achievement.

q: In a PSLC transaction, what does the buyer receive?
options: The underlying loan assets and credit risk
Fulfilment of the priority sector obligation, with no transfer of risk or loan assets
A share in the interest earned on the loan
explain: Only the obligation moves; the loans and risk stay with the seller.

q: On which RBI platform is the trading of priority sector lending certificates carried out?
explain: PSLCs are traded by banks on the RBI's e-Kuber portal.

q: Sub-prime lending refers to lending to borrowers who
options: Do not have a good credit history or do not meet normal credit appraisal standards
Have known the bank for more than ten years
Are not regular customers of any bank
explain: Sub-prime borrowers carry a weaker credit standing than prime borrowers.

q: The rate of interest that banks charge their major and prime customers is popularly called
explain: The Prime Lending Rate (PLR) is the rate for prime customers; repo and reverse repo are RBI policy rates.

q: An unsecured loan extended by one corporate to another is called
explain: Inter-corporate deposits (ICDs) are unsecured loans between corporates; commercial paper, T-bills and CDs are tradable instruments.

q: Which of the following would be treated as an unsecured loan?
explain: A personal loan is given without collateral, whereas housing and vehicle loans are secured against the asset.

q: Which aspects are outlined in the loan policy of a bank?
options: Rating standards, lending procedures and financial covenants
explain: A loan policy sets out rating standards, lending procedures and financial covenants for credit decisions.
